story.value: Polonium was discovered by Marie Sklodowska Curie, a Polish chemist, in 1898.
Polonium is named after Poland, the native country of Madame Curie.
Curie obtained polonium from pitchblende, a material that contains uranium.

uses.value: Polonium is used in brushes for removing dust from photographic films.
Polonium can be used to remove static electricity in machinery, such as machines that roll paper, wire or sheet metal.
Polonium has attracted attention as a possible lightweight heat source for thermoelectric power in space satellites.
